comments.author: @travellives
comments.text: Which part of life in St. Vincent and the Grenadines stayed with you most—the rebuilding, the farming communities or life at sea? If these islands are home to you, what would you add?

comments.author: @lifeonearth68
comments.text: Living on Bequia sounds peaceful until you realize even a doctor's appointment might mean taking a ferry to another island. Anyone from Bequia know how people manage when the sea is too rough for the boats to run? 😀😀

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Living on an island certainly requires a lot of flexibility, and it's always interesting to see how locals adapt their routines when the sea makes travel difficult! 😊

comments.author: @UnseenOutlands
comments.text: The recovery story of Union Island after Hurricane Beryl is one of the most moving parts of this documentary. Beyond rebuilding houses, how are families restoring their livelihoods, schools, and community spaces? What has been the biggest obstacle to recovery, and are local residents getting enough support to rebuild in ways that make their homes safer against future storms?

replies.author: @UnseenOutlands
replies.text: @travellives Nature remains an enigma that we humans cannot control.

replies.author: @travellives
replies.text: Families are restoring livelihoods through income support and business grants, while schools and services are being rebuilt with funding to improve resilience against future storms. ✨
